newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close shade higher, seen steady.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close shade higher, seen steady.

text.p: Argentine stocks pushed slightly higher Tuesday, supported by a rally in New York stocks and bonds ahead of results for the U.S. presidential elections, dealers said.
"The international context continued to underpin the bolsa, but the rise here was very modest because players are cautious and locked in some profits," said Jose Napoli of brokers Ignoto y Napoli.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV edged up 0.2 percent in selective trading to 583.53, stretching gains of 1.5 percent Monday and 2.6 percent last week.
Traders said the bolsa was bracing for a possible sharp pullback on Wall Street after the elections if the Democrats manage not only to win re-election, but to sweep Congress.

"There could be a backlash, but then it could go either way -- maybe a landslide for the Democrats will make everyone happy considering how well the markets have done in recent years," said an analyst at a U.S.-based brokerage.
Npoli saw resistance at 600 on the MerVal.
"However, if Wall Street takes us by surprise and keeps rising, those who squared off their positions may come scrambling back," he added.
The all-share index closed up 0.3 percent, with winners beating losers 37 to 17 an 23 issues closing flat.
Floor volume picked up to 18.8 million pesos from 15.2 million on Tuesday, while over-the-counter deals rose to 76.9 million pesos from 58.2 million on Tuesday.

Best blue-chip performers were carmaker Ciadea, up 3.3 percent, and power company Central Costanera and textile firm Alpargatas, both up 3.2 percent. Losers were led by steelmaker Acindar, construction stock Polledo and petrochemical concern Indupa, off 2.6 percent, 2.0 percent and 1.5 percent each.
